title: Yeast Pitch Rate vs Lag-Time Comparison
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:batch
| stats latest(pitch_cells_billion) as pitch_cells latest(volume_l) as volume_l latest(lag_hours) as lag_hours by batch style
| eval cells_per_l=round(pitch_cells/volume_l,1)
| sort lag_hours
description: Compares how heavily each batch was pitched against the time it took fermentation to get moving.
value: Lag time is one of the clearest early signals of yeast health, and comparing it with pitch rate helps refine future brew-day decisions.
implementation: Export batch metadata from your recipe tracker with pitch estimates and the first visible fermentation timestamp.
visualization: Scatter plot of pitch cells per litre versus lag hours.
grandmaExplanation: It watches how much yeast you used and how quickly each batch woke up, so you can learn what works best.
